;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[September 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
***Ten people are killed and 15 others injured in a [[roadside bomb]] attack in [[Kabul]] that targeted the first vice president, [[Amrullah Saleh]], who is wounded by the attack. The [[Taliban]] denied responsibility for the bombing. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-54084841 (BBC News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Oregon wildfires]]
**[[Governor of Oregon|Governor]] [[Kate Brown]] orders mass evacuations across [[Oregon|the state]] after reporting that a series of wildfires have "substantially destroyed" the cities and towns of [[Blue River, Oregon|Blue River]], [[Detroit, Oregon|Detroit]], [[Phoenix, Oregon|Phoenix]], [[Talent, Oregon|Talent]], and [[Vida, Oregon|Vida]]. Brown also enacts an emergency fire act to grant "immediate powers" to the state's fire officials. [https://www.deccanherald.com/international/world-news-politics/hundreds-of-oregon-homes-destroyed-by-us-wildfires-885187.html (AFP via ''Deccan Herald'')]
** Smoke impacts a wide swath of California and Oregon. [[San Francisco]] is particularly affected by the smoke floating south from the Oregon fires. [https://www.sfchronicle.com/california-wildfires/article/The-day-the-sun-didn-t-come-up-People-in-15554470.php#photo-19931093 (SF Chronicle)]
*Multiple fires erupt in the [[Mytilene#Moria|Mória Reception & Identification Centre]], [[Greece]]'s largest migrant camp, causing widespread destruction. The fires happen shortly after the entire camp was put under [[quarantine]] due to the detection of positive [[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece|COVID-19]] cases. [https://www.dw.com/en/greece-refugee-camp-fire/a-54861061 (DW)]
* [[Orange Skies Day]]
** Wildfire smoke from the [[2020 Oregon wildfires]] creates an orange skyline in the San Francisco Bay Area. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-54096319.amp (BBC)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****[[Portugal]] reports 646 new cases and three new deaths. It is the biggest daily increase in new cases since the national [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns|lockdown]] was lifted in May, bringing the cumulative totals to 61,541 confirmed cases and 1,849 deaths in 191 days since the first infections were identified. [https://www.rtp.pt/noticias/mundo/covid-19-a-situacao-ao-minuto-do-novo-coronavirus-no-pais-e-no-mundo_e1257647 (RTP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Slovenia]]
****[[Slovenia]] reports 79 cases, an all-time high. [https://www.rtvslo.si/zdravje/novi-koronavirus/vladna-krizna-skupina-brez-novih-ukrepov-za-omejevanje-sirjenja-koronavirusa/535580 (RTVSLO)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]]
****The number of new cases registered in the [[Netherlands]] surges to 1,140 in the last 24 hours, the highest daily total since April. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-netherlands-tally/new-dutch-coronavirus-cases-spike-to-1140-most-since-april-idUSKBN2601U4 (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[United Kingdom]] reports 2,659 cases, up from 2,460 a day earlier. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-britain-cases-idUSKBN2602EU (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
***[[Jakarta]] tightens its [[2020 Indonesia large-scale social restrictions|large-scale social restrictions]] in the province, which will take effect on September 14, due to the rise in new cases. All non-essential activities are ordered to be suspended and most workers, with the exception of 11 essential activities, are ordered to [[work from home]]. [https://megapolitan.kompas.com/read/2020/09/09/20093221/anies-tarik-rem-darurat-psbb-di-jakarta-kembali-seperti-awal-pandemi (''Kompas'')]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***[[AstraZeneca]] says that they might resume vaccine trials next week. This comes after the vaccine trial was put on hold due to a suspected adverse reaction the day before. [https://www.ft.com/content/98fca6d4-fcd2-488c-bcfc-d47758740a1a (''Financial Times'')]
*The latest publication of the [[Living Planet Index]] reports that the world's [[wildlife]] populations have decreased by an average of 68 percent between 1970 and 2016. The [[World Wide Fund for Nature]] cites the increasing [[deforestation]] and [[agricultural expansion]] for the population decline. [https://mb.com.ph/2020/09/10/world-wildlife-plummets-more-than-two-thirds-in-50-years-index/ (AFP via ''Manila Bulletin'')]

;International relations
*[[Iraq–United States relations]], [[Withdrawal of U.S. troops from Iraq (2020)]]
**[[United States Marine Corps]] general [[Kenneth F. McKenzie Jr.]] announces that the [[United States]] will reduce their troop presence in [[Iraq]] from 5,200 to 3,000. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/u-s-withdraw-more-2-000-troops-iraq-n1239598 (NBC News)]

;Law and crime
*[[2020–2021 United States racial unrest]], [[George Floyd protests]]
**[[George Floyd protests in Portland, Oregon]]
***Protesters and police clash near the [[Portland City Hall (Oregon)|Portland City Hall]] in [[Oregon]]. [[Portland Police Bureau]] announce that 11 arrests have been made. [https://www.startribune.com/clashes-in-portland-erupt-again-police-make-11-arrests/572358422/ (''The Star-Tribune'')]
*[[Yamil Abreu Navarro|Extradition of Yamil Abreu Navarro]]
**[[President of the Dominican Republic|Dominican Republic President]] [[Luis Abinader]] signs the [[extradition]] to the United States of [[Yamil Abreu Navarro]] on crimes of [[Illegal drug trade]]. Yamil Abreu Navarro is currently the leader of the ruling [[Modern Revolutionary Party]]. [https://dominicantoday.com/dr/local/2020/09/09/abinader-signs-extradition-of-major-capo/ (''Dominican Today'')]
*[[Sri Lanka]] announces legal action against the owner and manager of the [[MT New Diamond|MT ''New Diamond'']] ship which caught fire last Thursday off the coast of the country. Sri Lankan authorities say the lawsuit will be issued under the nation's law. Neither the owner nor manager of the ship commented on the statement. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-india-tanker-blast-legal/sri-lanka-to-take-legal-action-against-tankers-owner-after-fire-idUSKBN260128?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Russian interference in the 2020 United States elections]]
**Former [[Under Secretary of Homeland Security for Intelligence and Analysis]] Brian Murphy claims in a [[whistleblower]] reprisal complaint that Acting [[United States Secretary of Homeland Security|Secretary of Homeland Security]] [[Chad Wolf]] had instructed officials at [[United States Department of Homeland Security|the department]] to fabricate [[intelligence assessment]]s regarding the threat of Russian interference in the U.S. elections, which he claims is an effort by the [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] to understate the threat. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2020/sep/09/trump-whistleblower-russia-election-threat (''The Guardian'')]
*Citizens in [[Tigray Region]], [[Ethiopia]] begin casting their votes for a local election, defying the [[government of Ethiopia|central government]] and increasing political tensions. Tigray's authorities object the postponement of the August general election and the time of [[Prime Minister of Ethiopia|Prime Minister]] [[Abiy Ahmed]] in office, and say that any intervention by the government would amount to a "declaration of war". [https://apnews.com/d9bde847b216728d6f30d9c6fc7b79b9 (AP)]
